name: Shan Van Vocht

attributes.attribute: goddess of Sovereignty in her late form

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Shan Van Vocht is one name for the spéir-bhean, the sky woman of Irish story. She is a late form of the goddess of Sovereignty. By her right a king could hold Ireland. The bards of the 16th to 18th centuries drew her as a young beauty from the Otherworld. She walked the roads to seek out the true leader of the land. Writers gave her other names. One was Cathleen Ni Houlihan. Another was Roisin Dubh, the Dark Rosaleen. In the form of the Shan Van Vocht she is the poor old woman. This figure recalls the hag who becomes young again when the rightful ruler kisses her. The most famous telling stands in Yeats's play. That play shares her name with Maude Gonne, the woman who roused a nation to rise.
